conditions.description: The base image is referenced by the mutable python:3.13 tag without a digest.
conditions.rationale: A later build can resolve the same Dockerfile text to different base-image bytes.

conditions.description: ADD fetches a remote executable URL without a content digest or checksum in the Dockerfile.
conditions.rationale: The build trusts mutable network content for an executable artifact without binding exact bytes.

conditions.description: pip installs requests and flask without version pins or hashes.
conditions.rationale: Dependency resolution can change over time and does not establish the exact installed package set.

conditions.description: The Dockerfile never switches away from the default root user.
conditions.rationale: The resulting container command runs as root unless an external runtime overrides the user.

conditions.description: The Dockerfile sets an explicit WORKDIR before application commands.
conditions.rationale: An inspector should not report that the container has no declared working directory.

conditions.description: The final CMD uses exec-form JSON syntax.
conditions.rationale: The fixture should not be falsely reported as using shell-form CMD for its main process.

conditions.description: Whether the build environment enforces signed or allowlisted base images is not established by the Dockerfile.
conditions.rationale: Registry admission and signature verification are external build controls.

conditions.description: Whether deployment policy overrides the container user to a non-root UID is not established here.
conditions.rationale: Runtime securityContext or platform policy is outside the image definition.

conditions.description: The image build must not be cleared as reproducible from the Dockerfile alone.
conditions.rationale: The base image, remote executable, and Python packages are all resolved without immutable content identities.

conditions.description: The image must not be cleared as having established end-to-end supply-chain integrity.
conditions.rationale: Remote executable content and dependencies are unbound, while external signing policy remains unknown.
